definition: Tradable credits that let owners of renewable generation sell the renewable attribute of their electricity separately from the electricity itself.
core_idea: RECs give renewable generators a second income stream by letting them sell the environmental/renewable attribute of their power, and are commonly purchased by load-serving entities to satisfy renewable-acquisition obligations; they also let a grid track how much renewable generation has actually been delivered.
key_points: RECs are often purchased by load-serving entities to meet obligations to acquire specified amounts of renewable energy.
RECs provide a second source of income to renewable generators such as wind and solar producers.
REC markets provide a way to track renewable contributions once power is placed onto the grid.
In a deregulated market, the REC market is described as a way to incentivize construction of new renewable generation.
relationships: Complements PPAs as a renewable-generation revenue/procurement mechanism.
trading_implications: Renewable generators can monetize RECs independently of their energy sales, and buyers (e.g., load-serving entities) may need to source RECs separately from energy to meet compliance obligations.
caveats: A REC represents the renewable attribute of power, not the power itself — a buyer of RECs is not necessarily buying the underlying electricity.
